title: Overhaul minor drive train components on agricultural equipment

lessons.title: Minor drive train parts and planning the overhaul
lessons.html:
What are minor drive train components?

Minor drive train parts are the smaller parts that carry power on tractors and implements. You can overhaul them in the farm workshop. Examples are:

  • universal joints (UJs) on PTO shafts and drive shafts;
  • PTO shafts and their shear bolts or slip clutches;
  • clutch release bearings and clutch linkages;
  • chain drives and sprockets on planters and balers;
  • V-belt drives and pulleys on slashers and mixers;
  • wheel bearings and hubs on trailers and implements.

Overhaul means taking the part apart, cleaning it, checking every piece, replacing worn pieces and putting it back so it works like new.

Planning

  1. Read the job card. Find out what the fault is: noise, play, slipping, or heat.
  2. Look up the part in the manual. Note the torque values, clearances and the grease or oil to use.
  3. Get an overhaul kit or the new parts: bearings, seals, circlips, crosses.
  4. Get the right tools: circlip pliers, pullers, a press, soft hammer, feeler gauges, torque wrench.

Safety

  • Switch off the tractor, take out the key and make sure the PTO is off before you touch any drive part.
  • Lower implements to the ground or block them up safely.
  • Wear safety glasses when using circlips – they can fly out at your eyes.
  • A PTO shaft can kill. It can catch loose clothing and pull you in. Never work on or step over a turning PTO shaft. Always fit the PTO guard back after the job.

lessons.title: Taking apart, checking and replacing worn pieces
lessons.html:
Taking apart

  1. Clean the outside of the part.
  2. Mark the parts with a punch or paint before you take them apart. For example, mark the two halves of a PTO shaft so the yokes line up again.
  3. Remove circlips with circlip pliers.
  4. Use a puller or a press to remove bearings and gears. Never hit a bearing directly with a steel hammer.
  5. Lay all parts out in order on a clean bench.

Checking each piece

PartLook for
UJ cross and cupsPlay, rust, rough turning, worn needle rollers
BearingsRough or noisy when turned, blue colour, pitting
ChainsStretched links, stiff links, rust
SprocketsHooked or pointed teeth
PulleysWorn or shiny grooves, cracks
SealsHard, cracked or torn lips
ShaftsBent, worn splines, scoring where seals run

Measure parts with a vernier or feeler gauges where the manual gives limits. If the part is outside the limit, replace it.

Replace in sets

Some parts must be changed together. A new chain on worn sprockets wears out fast, so change chain and sprockets together. Change V-belts as a matched set. Always fit new seals and new circlips.

lessons.title: Reassembling, adjusting and testing
lessons.html:
Reassembling

  1. Clean all parts you will reuse.
  2. Pack bearings and UJ cups with the grease the manual names.
  3. Press bearings in by the correct ring: press on the outer ring when fitting into a housing, and on the inner ring when fitting onto a shaft.
  4. Fit new seals the right way round, with the lip facing the oil or grease.
  5. Fit circlips fully into their grooves. Check by turning them.
  6. Line up your marks so parts go back in the same position.
  7. Tighten bolts and nuts to the torque in the manual.

Adjusting

  • Chains – set the slack as the manual says. Too tight wears the chain; too loose lets it jump.
  • Belts – set the tension. Line up the pulleys with a straight edge.
  • Wheel bearings – set the end play as the manual shows and fit a new split pin.
  • Clutch linkage – set the free play on the pedal.

Testing

Fit all guards back first. Then, with everyone standing clear, run the drive slowly. Check:

  • no strange noises or vibration;
  • no heat at bearings after a short run (feel carefully once stopped and switched off);
  • no leaks of grease or oil;
  • chains and belts run straight.

Record the parts used and the work done on the job card.

Key points

  • Switch off and make sure the PTO is off before touching drive parts.
  • Mark parts before you take them apart and lay them out in order.
  • Replace chains with sprockets, belts in sets, and always use new seals and circlips.
  • Adjust chains, belts and bearings to the manual.
  • Put every guard back before testing.
